item.title: Experimental Statistical and Explainable Machine Learning Prediction of Surface Roughness in Cryogenically Pre-Cooled Machining of Inconel 718
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 C S Sumesh
Cryogenic machining offers a sustainable route for improving the machinability of nickel-based superalloys by reducing thermal loading and improving surface quality. This study develops an experimental-statistical-explainable machine learning framework for predicting surface roughness during cryogenically pre-cooled machining of Inconel 718. Spindle speed, feed rate, and depth of cut were varied through a 20-run face-centered central composite design. Each trial was repeated three times, and surface roughness was measured at three locations. The response surface model explained 91.95% of the measured variation and was used to generate a 1,387-point model-based dataset. item.title: Band-Resolved Superconducting Gaps via the Thermal Hall Effect in CeRu2
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Darian Hall, Luke Pritchard Cairns, Nico Rowland, Yuanqi Lyu, Kohtaro Yamakawa, Josue Rodriguez, Kirin Chanteloup, Didier Perrodin, Joel E. Moore, James G. Analytis
arXiv:2610.22361v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Standard bulk probes of multiband superconductors cannot assign pairing gaps to specific electron or hole Fermi surfaces. Here we show that thermal Hall transport (κₓy), constrained by specific heat and normal-state magnetotransport, resolves this ambiguity in the compensated heavy-fermion superconductor CeRu₂. Fixing the gap magnitudes (Δₑ/k_Bapprox 13K, Δₕ/k_Bapprox 8K) and band mobilities completely determines the electronic degrees of freedom in κₓₓ and κₓy. A low-field sign reversal in κₓy places the larger gap on the heavy Ce 4f electron sheets and the smaller on the hole sheets.
